1. Executive Summary

What SecretSifter does and why it matters.

SecretSifter is a Burp Suite extension for passive and active detection of secrets exposed in HTTP traffic. It integrates directly into the Burp proxy pipeline — no configuration required — and begins reporting findings immediately after installation.

Modern web applications leak credentials in JavaScript bundles, configuration endpoints, API responses, and request headers. Manual review of this traffic is impractical at scale. SecretSifter automates the detection layer using a multi-phase scan engine: anchored vendor token patterns, Shannon entropy heuristics, context-gated rules, and PII validators — filtering out noise while surfacing real, actionable secrets.

Findings appear as AuditIssues in Burp's Dashboard (Pro) and in the Bulk Scan results table (all editions), with severity classification, matched value preview, and one-click HTML/CSV export for reporting.

Community Edition: Passive scan check (Dashboard → Issue Activity) requires Burp Suite Professional. All other features — Bulk Scan, right-click rescan, proxy handler, sitemap sweep, HAR import, and reports — work in Community Edition.

2. Problems SecretSifter Solves

The security problems this tool addresses.

ProblemHow SecretSifter Solves It
Secrets in JS bundles
API keys, tokens, and service credentials embedded in React/Vue/Angular bundles and shipped to every browser visitor.		 Passive scan fires on every proxied response. Bulk Scan follows <script src> and webpack chunks. HTML inline script blocks are extracted and scanned separately.
Credentials in API responses
Config endpoints (/api/config, /__env) returning keys in JSON that are not meant to be client-accessible.		 JSON body walker traverses all key-value pairs at every depth. SSR state blobs (Next.js __NEXT_DATA__, Nuxt __NUXT__) are detected and unwrapped.
Credentials in request headers
Custom authentication headers (App_key, Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key, Resource) that are client-controlled and potentially over-privileged.		 Request header scanning (opt-in) checks custom headers for high-value credential patterns across every proxied request.
PII in responses
Social Security Numbers or credit card numbers appearing in API responses, error pages, or debug output.		 PII scanner with Luhn validation (cards) and SSN format checks. Runs in FULL tier; toggle in Settings.
Dynamic SPA API calls missed by static scan
XHR/Fetch calls only made after JavaScript executes — invisible in the site map until the page is actually visited.		 Headless Browse launches Chrome/Chromium through Burp proxy to capture dynamic calls. Scope Monitor captures passive findings from browsed sessions and routes them into the Bulk Scan table.
Authenticated or offline content
Responses captured in HAR files from authenticated sessions that cannot be replayed.		 HAR import scans responses from .har files directly — no live HTTP fetch required.
High false positive rate
Entropy-based scanners produce noise on obfuscated CSS class names, UUIDs, and webpack hashes.		 60+ noise key-name filters, Angular/Vue directive suppression, UUID rejection, JWT body suppression, Luhn validation, CDN blocklist, and user-configurable key name blocklist/allowlist.

3.1 Passive Scanning

Once loaded, SecretSifter hooks into the Burp proxy pipeline and scans every response body that passes through the proxy. The proxy handler fires on all traffic — not scope-limited — so secrets in third-party API calls are also captured.

On extension load, a background thread sweeps all responses already present in Burp's Target → Site Map, so findings appear immediately even for traffic captured before the extension was installed. This sweep runs once per session on a daemon thread and exits cleanly on unload.

3.2 Bulk Scan

The Bulk Scan tab accepts a list of target URLs and fetches them concurrently (1–50 threads). For each URL it can follow <script src> references and webpack chunk manifests (depth 1), optionally launching a headless Chrome instance to capture dynamic XHR/Fetch calls that only fire after JavaScript executes.

3.3 HAR File Import

SecretSifter can scan HTTP Archive (.har) files directly from the Bulk Scan tab. Use this when:

  • The target requires authentication that cannot be replayed by the extension.
  • You have responses captured in another tool (browser DevTools, Charles Proxy) and want to scan offline.
  • The target is not accessible from the Burp machine (e.g. internal staging environments captured during an on-site engagement).

Import a .har file using the Import button in the Bulk Scan tab. SecretSifter reads the response.content.text field from each HAR entry and runs the full scan pipeline against it without making any network requests.

3.4 Scan Tiers

TierRules ActiveUse When
FAST100+ anchored vendor tokens onlyQuick recon, large site maps, passive scan on high-traffic sites.
LIGHT+ High-entropy scanner + 40+ context-gated rules + DB connection stringsStandard penetration test — good balance of speed and coverage.
FULL+ PII (SSN, CC) + Generic KV + SSR state blobs + JSON walker + getter functionsDeep audit, bug bounty, maximum coverage.

CategoryCountExamples

Context-gated rules40+Algolia API key (near "algolia"), Cloudflare token, Zendesk token, Heroku key, Datadog key, Salesforce token, Auth0 client secret

3.6 AI Triage

SecretSifter supports three AI triage providers, configured in Settings → AI Triage:

  • Burp AI — Burp Suite's built-in AI (Professional + AI features enabled in Burp Settings → AI). Uses the Burp AI prompt API; no external API key needed.
  • Anthropic API — Direct call to Claude (Sonnet 4.x or later) using your Anthropic API key. Works in Community Edition.
  • OpenAI / compatible — Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, local Ollama, etc.). Configure endpoint URL, API key, and model name.

Two triage modes are available for all providers:

  • Per-finding: Right-click any finding → AI Triage.
  • AI Triage All: Bulk button in the Bulk Scan tab. Findings are sent in batches of 15. After triage, noise candidates are highlighted amber and a review dialog lets you delete or keep them.

Burp AI requires Burp Suite Professional with AI features enabled. Anthropic and OpenAI providers work in any edition with a valid API key entered in Settings → AI Triage.

Step-by-step instructions for all scan modes.

4.1 Installation

Step 1 — Choose Your JAR

JAREntry PointUse When
secretsifter-store-*.jarSecretScannerExtensionStoreStandard use, BApp Store install. No embedded HTTP server.
secretsifter-mcp-*.jarSecretScannerExtensionClaude Code / MCP agent integration. Starts JSON-RPC server on 127.0.0.1:8765.

Step 2 — Load into Burp Suite

  1. Open Burp Suite → Extensions tab → Installed → Add
  2. Set Extension type: Java
  3. Browse to your chosen JAR file
  4. Click Next — the extension loads and a Secret Sifter tab appears
  5. Check Extensions → Output for the version confirmation line:

4.2 Passive Scanning (Automatic)

No action required. Once loaded, the extension scans all responses flowing through the Burp proxy. Findings appear in:

  • Dashboard → Issue Activity — as Burp AuditIssues (Pro only)
  • Target → Site Map — under the target host with a SecretSifter issue icon
  • Secret Sifter → Bulk Scan results table (all editions)
  • SecretSifter tab in Proxy History / Repeater — findings for the selected response

4.3 Bulk Scan Workflow

  1. Navigate to Secret Sifter → Bulk Scan
  2. Paste one URL per line, or import a .txt / .csv / .har file
  3. Configure scan options (see table below)
  4. Click ▶ Start Scan
  5. Findings populate the table in real time, sorted by severity
  6. Click Export → HTML Report, HTML Report (per domain), or CSV

5. Detection Engine Deep Dive

How the scan pipeline works under the hood.

5.1 Scan Pipeline

For each response body, SecretSifter runs a multi-phase pipeline. Phases run in order; each phase can be toggled by scan tier:

Input: response body (string) + Content-Type + source URL
  │
  1. Content-type gate — skip binary, image, video, audio, font responses
  2. HTML inline script extraction — extract text content of <script> blocks
  3. Anchored token scan (FAST+) — vendor-specific regex against raw body
  4. Context-gated scan (LIGHT+) — keyword proximity check then regex
  5. DB connection string scan (LIGHT+) — URI pattern with embedded credentials
  6. High-entropy KV scan (LIGHT+) — key=value pairs with entropy ≥ threshold
  7. SSR state blob unwrap (FULL) — parse JSON blobs, then re-run pipeline
  8. JSON walker (FULL) — recursive key-value traversal of JSON bodies
  9. PII scan (FULL) — SSN, credit card, credential URLs
 10. Getter function scan (FULL) — return "secret_value" patterns in JS
  │
 Output: List<SecretFinding>

5.2 Anchored Vendor Token Rules (100+)

Anchored rules use vendor-documented format specifications. Each rule has a regex with a fixed prefix that uniquely identifies the vendor (e.g. ghp_ for GitHub PATs, sk- for OpenAI keys). This makes the pattern highly specific with near-zero false positive rate.

VendorToken TypePattern Prefix
GitHubPersonal Access Tokenghp_, gho_, ghu_, ghs_, ghr_
GitLabPersonal / Project tokenglpat-, glptt-
AWSAccess Key IDAKIA, ASIA, AROA
StripeSecret / Restricted keysk_live_, rk_live_
OpenAIAPI keysk-proj-, sk-
SlackBot / App tokenxoxb-, xapp-, xoxe-
ShopifyPartner / Store tokenshpss_, shppa_, shpat_
AzureStorage / SAS keyFormat-matched 64-char base64 or SAS token structure
GCPService account key IDEmbedded in JSON key files
Docker HubAccess tokendckr_pat_
ClerkSecret keysk_live_ + Clerk-specific format
…and 90+ more

5.3 Context-Gated Rules (40+)

Context-gated rules require a vendor keyword to appear in proximity (within ~200 characters) before the value pattern is triggered. This prevents the high entropy value from matching unrelated content.

Example: Algolia API key rule only triggers if algolia appears near a 32-character alphanumeric string. Without the proximity check, any 32-char string would match.

Vendors covered include: Algolia, Cloudflare, Zendesk, Heroku, Datadog, Salesforce, Mistral, Cohere, Auth0, Supabase, Pinecone, Twilio, SendGrid, Mailchimp, Mailgun, and more.

5.4 False Positive Reduction

MitigationWhat It Prevents
60+ noise key-name filter (NOISE_KEYNAMES)Keys ending in Type, Error, State, Version, etc. — discriminator enums, not secrets.
UUID rejection8-4-4-4-12 format UUIDs filtered out unless key name ends in Secret or Token.
Angular / Vue directive filterStrings matching Angular expression or Vue directive syntax (v-, ng-) suppressed.
JWT body suppressionJWT payload segment (the middle eyJ… block) filtered — this is base64 JSON metadata, not a secret.
Encoding alphabet filterValues composed entirely of characters common in CSS hex colors, base64 padding, or webpack hashes are suppressed.
CC floating-point guard16-digit sequences that are clearly floating-point numbers (contain a decimal) are not reported as credit card numbers.
CDN blocklistResponses from common CDN domains (jQuery, Bootstrap, Analytics) are skipped entirely.
Luhn validationCredit card candidates must pass the Luhn checksum algorithm.
Key name blocklist (user-configurable)Any key name matching a user-defined substring pattern is suppressed.
Key name allowlist (user-configurable)Key names matching allowlist patterns bypass entropy thresholds and are always reported.

6. Severity & Confidence Model

How findings are scored and what each level means for triage.

6.1 Severity Levels

LevelMeaningTypical Finding
HIGHConfirmed active credential — rotate immediately.GitHub PAT, AWS Access Key, Stripe live secret key, OpenAI API key.
MEDIUMToken that confirms a live service integration.Algolia search key, Cloudflare API token, Auth0 client secret.
LOWIdentifier or key with limited standalone risk.Public bucket name, CDN zone ID, analytics measurement ID.
INFORMATIONStructural or schema-level finding.DB connection string without credentials, JWT header.

6.2 Confidence Levels

ConfidenceBasis
CERTAINAnchored rule with vendor-documented format — false positive is theoretically impossible.
FIRMContext-gated rule or DB connection string — vendor keyword in proximity confirms intent.
TENTATIVEEntropy heuristic or generic KV rule — possible false positive; verify manually.

7. Triage Guide & Error Cases

How to investigate, validate, and resolve common issues.

7.1 Validating a Finding

Severity / ConfidenceValidation Steps
HIGH / CERTAIN
  1. Check the source URL — is it a production endpoint?
  2. Confirm the value appears in the live response (Burp Response tab in Advisory panel).
  3. For API keys: attempt a minimal API call to verify the key is active (in scope of your engagement).
  4. For AWS keys: run aws sts get-caller-identity to check if active.
  5. Export the SecretSifter HTML report — it includes a masked value preview and context snippet.
MEDIUM / FIRM
  1. Examine the key name and matched value in the finding detail.
  2. Check the source URL path — config.js, app-config.json suggest real config.
  3. Run AI Triage (Pro) — Burp's AI can confirm or downgrade the finding.
  4. If the value looks like a vendor's own demo key, mark as false positive.
LOW / TENTATIVE Verify the identifier is credential-bearing (e.g. an Algolia key that allows write queries). If it grants no sensitive access, document as informational.

7.2 Common Error Conditions

SymptomLikely CauseResolution
Extension does not load Burp version < 2024.7 or loading the plain compile JAR Verify Burp ≥ 2024.7. Load secretsifter-store-*.jar or secretsifter-mcp-*.jar — not a plain class file. Check Extensions → Output.
No findings for a known secret Scan tier too low, JS file not fetched, or traffic not flowing through proxy
  1. Switch Settings → Scan Tier to FULL.
  2. Enable Follow <script src> and Follow webpack chunks in Bulk Scan.
  3. Browse the target through Burp Browser, then click Scan Site Map.
  4. For headers: enable Scan request headers in Settings.
Burp slows during passive scan FULL tier entropy scan on high-volume CDN traffic Switch to FAST tier. Expand CDN blocklist. Disable PII scanning.
Bulk scan finds secrets but Target → Site Map shows nothing Directly-fetched JS files have no site map entry; Burp "Hiding not found items" filter hides them Browse the target through Burp Browser first — this seeds the site map root URL. SecretSifter then files issues at the root URL so they appear in the site map.
Headless Browse does nothing / Chrome not found Chrome / Chromium not installed or not on PATH Install Google Chrome or Chromium. On macOS, /Applications/Google Chrome.app is auto-detected. Check Extensions → Output for [Headless] Chrome/Chromium not found.
AI Triage All button greyed out Community Edition, or AI features disabled Go to Burp Settings → AI → uncheck Disable AI features. Reload the extension.
Findings in Bulk Scan but not in Dashboard Dashboard → Issue Activity requires Burp Pro All findings are in the Bulk Scan table and HTML/CSV export in both editions.
High false positive rate from entropy scanner Entropy threshold too low, or target uses obfuscated keys Increase entropy threshold to 4.0–4.5 in Settings. Add FP-prone key names to Key Name Blocklist.
Same finding reported multiple times Extension reloaded mid-session; deduplicator cleared on reload Deduplication is session-scoped. Each session deduplicates within itself. Reload Burp or unload/reload the extension to reset.
MCP Bridge won't start Port 8765 in use, or using the store JAR instead of the MCP JAR Ensure you loaded secretsifter-mcp-*.jar. Check that port 8765 is free (lsof -i :8765). Enable MCP Bridge in Settings → MCP Bridge.
MCP: no response from Claude after claude mcp add Claude Code was not restarted after registering the MCP server Exit Claude Code and reopen it (or start a new session). MCP servers are loaded only at session start — a running session won't pick up a newly registered server.

7.3 False Positive Determination Guide

PatternFP IndicatorAction
Value contains example, YOUR_KEY, xxxx, changemeDocumentation placeholderShould be auto-filtered; if not, add key name to blocklist.
Source URL is a CDN (cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com)Open-source library — vendor's own demo keyAdd domain to CDN Blocklist in Settings.
Value is a valid UUID (8-4-4-4-12 format)Azure tenant/client ID — not a secretAuto-filtered unless key name ends in Secret or Token.
Key name ends in Type, Error, StateEnum / type discriminatorAuto-filtered by noise key-name list.
Source URL is test., dev., staging.Non-production credential — lower riskDocument as out-of-scope risk; rotate if same key is used in production.

8.3 Initialization Sequence

initialize(MontoyaApi api)
 │
 1. ScanSettings           ← load from Burp Preferences
 2. SecretScanner          ← stateless engine, injected with settings
 3. SecretScanCheck        ← register passive scan check (Pro only; gracefully skipped)
 4. SecretProxyHandler     ← register proxy response handler (all traffic)
 5. SecretContextMenu      ← register right-click menu provider
 6. SecretSifterTab        ← register inline HTTP response tab
 7. SettingsPanel +
    BulkScanPanel          ← register single "Secret Sifter" top-level tab
 8. loadFromPreferences()  ← sync persisted settings to UI
 9. McpBridge.start()      ← optional; only if MCP enabled (mcp build only)
10. SitemapSweep thread    ← daemon thread, starts after 1.5 s, scans existing site map
11. registerUnloadingHandler ← clean shutdown of all threads/executors

8.4 Four Scan Entry Points

Entry PointHow It TriggersScope
Passive scan checkEvery proxied response, via Burp's scanner APIIn-scope only (Burp Pro)
Proxy handlerEvery proxy response, background threadAll traffic, cross-origin aware
Right-click rescanUser selects "Rescan for Secrets" in context menuSelected host + full site map
Bulk scanUser pastes URL list, 1–50 concurrent threadsUser-specified URLs + following

8.5 Thread Safety Model

  • SecretScanner is fully stateless — safe for concurrent calls from any thread
  • ScanSettings uses volatile fields for primitives; synchronized methods for list operations
  • seenRequestValues (cross-request dedup) uses Collections.synchronizedSet()
  • currentTargetUrl uses ThreadLocal; hostToTargetUrl uses ConcurrentHashMap
  • SitemapDeduplicator uses two ConcurrentHashMap instances — separate namespaces for bulk scan and proxy handler
  • Proxy handler submits scan work to a fixed-size ExecutorService — the proxy pipeline is never blocked

10. Building from Source

Instructions for developers and security teams who need to build from source.

10.1 Prerequisites

RequirementVersionNotes
Java JDK17+Bundled with Burp Suite, or install separately (brew install openjdk@17)
Gradle8+Use the included wrapper (./gradlew) — no system install required
GitAnyFor cloning the repository

10.2 Clone and Build

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/secretsifter/secretsifter-burp
cd secretsifter-burp

# Build the store JAR (BApp Store — no MCP server)
./gradlew shadowJar
# Output: build/libs/secretsifter-store-<version>.jar

# Build the full JAR (includes McpBridge for Claude Code integration)
./gradlew shadowJarFull
# Output: build/libs/secretsifter-mcp-<version>.jar

# Build both JARs in one step
./gradlew buildAll

# Run tests
./gradlew test
# Test report: build/reports/tests/test/index.html

Two JARs, two entry points:
secretsifter-store-*.jar — entry point SecretScannerExtensionStore. No embedded HTTP listener. For BApp Store and community distribution.

secretsifter-mcp-*.jar — entry point SecretScannerExtension. Includes McpBridge JSON-RPC server on 127.0.0.1:8765 for Claude Code / MCP agent integration.
